questions.def: Use past perfect for actions completed before another past action.
questions.question: By the time I arrived, the movie ___.

questions.def: Use 'would' for reported future events in the past.
questions.question: She said she ___ call later.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had worked' for action before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ there before he moved abroad.

questions.def: Use past continuous for an action in progress in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to the radio when she called.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had' shows duration up to a past point.
questions.question: They ___ known each other for years.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous emphasizes duration before a past event.
questions.question: She ___ for hours when he finally arrived.

questions.def: Past perfect for action completed before another past action.
questions.question: The rain ___ when we left the house.

questions.def: Use 'had seen' to show experience before a past event.
questions.question: I ___ that movie before, so I didn't enjoy it.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had lived' for duration before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ in London for 5 years before moving.

questions.def: Use past perfect for action completed before a past point.
questions.question: He ___ the report before the deadline.

questions.def: Past continuous 'was listening' for action in progress.
questions.question: She ___ to the news on the radio yesterday.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous emphasizes duration before a past event.
questions.question: She ___ all night before the exam.

questions.def: Use past continuous for interrupted action in the past.
questions.question: I ___ the email when the power went out.

questions.def: Past perfect for action completed before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ home before it started to rain.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had travelled' action before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ around Europe before settling down.

questions.def: Past continuous shows an action in progress at a past time.
questions.question: The children ___ when I got home.

questions.def: Simple past 'submitted' for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: He ___ the report yesterday.

questions.def: 'Has' should be 'had' for the past perfect tense.
questions.question: She has finished her work before he arrived.

questions.def: Simple past 'rained' for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: It ___ all day yesterday.

questions.def: Past perfect shows experience prior to a past action.
questions.question: Before I met him, I ___ to Japan.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had already started' action before arrival.
questions.question: The concert ___ by the time we got there.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had cleaned' action before another past action.
questions.question: She ___ the house before the guests arrived.

questions.def: Past continuous 'was listening' for interrupted action.
questions.question: She ___ to the news when I interrupted her.

questions.def: Simple past 'met' for finished action at a specific past time.
questions.question: I ___ him at the conference last year.

questions.def: Use past perfect to show action completed before another past action.
questions.question: By the time I arrived, the movie ___ already.

questions.def: Use 'would' for future in the past after a past tense reporting verb.
questions.question: She said she ___ come to the party.

questions.def: 'is understanding' should be 'understood' (passive) or 'understands'.
questions.question: He had been thinking that he is understanding it now.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous emphasizes duration before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ for hours when the bus finally appeared.

questions.def: Past continuous describes an action in progress at a specific time.
questions.question: He ___ to the radio when the news broke.

questions.def: Past perfect passive to express completed action before a past time.
questions.question: By yesterday, all flights ___ cancelled.
